subtitle: When a Kashmiri Poet Put Kings on Trial

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot in a dim Kashmiri study, lamp-light catching dust as Kalhana bends over a palm-leaf manuscript
panels.action: Kalhana sits cross-legged beside a low desk piled with palm-leaf bundles and loose copper coins, his stylus poised, eyes fixed in fierce, thoughtful concentration in a scholarly household of 12th-century Kashmir.

dialogue.text: In 1148, in troubled Kashmir, Kalhana begins the Rajatarangini—vowing to judge long-dead kings like a witness in court, even while drowning in their legends.

i18n.hi: ११४८ में संकटग्रस्त कश्मीर में कल्हण राजतरंगिणी शुरू करता है—कसम खाकर कि सदियों पुराने राजाओं को अदालत के गवाह की तरह परखेगा, चाहे खुद उनकी कथाओं में डूबता रहे।

panels.shot: slow push-in from window to interior, showing Kalhana and the world outside
panels.action: Seen through a carved wooden lattice, Kalhana writes while outside, saffron-robed monks, armed retainers, and townsfolk move along a street under snow-dusted mountains.

dialogue.text: Three centuries after the Karkotas, Kashmir is smaller, fractured, yet full of memories. Inside his room, Kalhana tries to gather them into a single river of kings.

i18n.hi: कार्कोटों के तीन सौ साल बाद, कश्मीर छोटा, टूटा‑फूटा है, पर यादों से भरा। अपने कमरे में कल्हण इन्हें जोड़कर एक ही राजाओं की नदी बनाने की कोशिश करता है।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of Kalhana’s hand hovering over the manuscript leaves
panels.action: Kalhana’s hand hovers above a fresh palm leaf, stylus ready, beside neatly stacked bundles labeled with knotted cords and weighed down by a small stone.

dialogue.text: He opens his Rajatarangini with a promise: the worthy poet must tell the past as a judge does, free from attachment and aversion.

i18n.hi: वह राजतरंगिणी एक वचन से खोलता है: सच्चा कवि अतीत को न्यायाधीश की तरह कहे—राग‑द्वेष से मुक्त।

panels.shot: profile close-up of Kalhana, lamp-light on his face, background fading into darkness
panels.action: Kalhana sits in profile, lips slightly parted, eyes distant, as if weighing unseen testimonies in his mind while the lamp burns low beside him.

dialogue.speaker: kalhana
dialogue.text: If I praise, let it be earned. If I blame, let it be proved.

i18n.hi: जो स्तुति हो, वो कमाई हुई हो। जो निंदा हो, वो साबित हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of the study covered with different kinds of evidence
panels.action: The room is scattered with palm-leaf rolls, a worn copy of a Purana, a few copper and silver coins, and a rubbing of an inscription stone, all arranged around Kalhana.

dialogue.text: He tells us his tools: older chronicles, old tales, the Nilamata Purana, coins, inscriptions, and ruins still standing in the Valley.

i18n.hi: वह अपने औज़ार गिनता है: पुराने इतिहास, लोककथाएँ, नीलमत पुराण, सिक्के, शिलालेख, और घाटी में अब भी खड़ी इमारतों के खंडहर।

panels.shot: tight close-up on coins and inscription rubbing under Kalhana’s fingers
panels.action: Kalhana’s fingers rest on a line of Sharada script on a paper rubbing, while nearby a coin with a faint king’s figure glints in the lamplight.

dialogue.text: Material things do not flatter. Coins, carved stones, fallen walls—these are the hard edges against which he tests every story.

i18n.hi: जिंसा सामान चापलूसी नहीं करता। सिक्के, तराशे पत्थर, ढही दीवारें—इन्हीं सख्त किनारों से वह हर कहानी को रगड़कर परखता है।

panels.shot: imaginative split-scene: Kalhana small at bottom, vast ruins of Martand rising above in his mind’s eye
panels.action: Above Kalhana’s bowed head, the imagined pillars and colonnades of an ancient Sun temple rise vast against the sky, worn yet majestic, dwarfing his figure.

dialogue.text: When he writes of the Karkotas, he can still look up at Martand’s columns and Parihasapura’s broken halls, and ask: what kind of kings raised such stone?

i18n.hi: जब वह कार्कोटों की बात लिखता है, तो अब भी मार्तंड के स्तंभों और परिहासपुर के टूटे महलों को देख सकता है, और पूछ सकता है: ऐसे पत्थर किस तरह के राजा ने उठवाए थे?

panels.shot: medium shot of Kalhana listening to an elder storyteller in a courtyard
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard, an old Kashmiri man gestures as he speaks, while younger listeners sit around; Kalhana sits attentive, a palm-leaf on his lap.

dialogue.text: Some sources are living voices. Kalhana hears elders repeat tales of Lalitaditya’s conquests, of councils, intrigues, and disasters that left scars on families.

i18n.hi: कुछ स्रोत ज़िंदा आवाज़ें हैं। कल्हण बुज़ुर्गों को सुनता है, जो ललितादित्य की विजयों, सभाओं, षड्यंत्रों और उन हादसों के किस्से दोहराते हैं, जिनकी चोट परिवारों पर रह गई।

panels.shot: close-up of Kalhana’s thoughtful face reacting to a boastful tale
panels.action: Kalhana tilts his head, brows slightly furrowed, as if tasting each word, separating wonder from likelihood, while the storyteller’s hand is frozen mid-boast.

dialogue.text: He knows stories swell in the telling. In his prologue, he warns that mere poetry, without sources, often turns kings into giants and miracles.

i18n.hi: उसे पता है कि किस्से सुनते‑सुनते फूल जाते हैं। भूमिका में वह चेतावनी देता है: बिना स्रोत की सूखी कविता अक्सर राजाओं को राक्षस और चमत्कार बना देती है।

panels.shot: dim interior shot, Kalhana comparing two palm-leaf chronicles
panels.action: Kalhana kneels before two open bundles of leaves, his finger moving between differing lines, small weights keeping each manuscript open.

dialogue.text: Earlier court chronicles lie before him, now lost to us. He checks them against each other, noting where dates clash and flattery grows too thick.

i18n.hi: पुराने दरबारी इतिहास उसके सामने पड़े हैं, जो अब हमारे लिए खो चुके हैं। वह उन्हें एक‑दूसरे से मिला‑जुलाकर देखता है, जहाँ तारीखें भिड़ती हैं और चापलूसी ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा मोटी हो जाती है, वहाँ निशान लगाता है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder view of Kalhana writing the famous lines about a judge
panels.action: Seen from behind, we watch Kalhana carve careful, even letters into a fresh leaf, the words lined neatly, his wrist steady above the script.

dialogue.text: So he sets his rule: as a judge weighs witnesses, so he will weigh his sources, seeking agreement, noting doubt, refusing to bend for fear or favour.

i18n.hi: तब वह अपना नियम ठोकता है: जैसे न्यायाधीश गवाहों को तौलता है, वैसे ही वह अपने स्रोतों को तौलेगा—जहाँ सहमति हो उसे मानेगा, जहाँ शक हो दर्ज करेगा, और डर या मेहरबानी में झुकने से इंकार करेगा।

panels.shot: low-angle shot, Kalhana silhouetted against shelves and rolled manuscripts
panels.action: Kalhana stands, stretching his back, surrounded by stacked manuscripts and hanging scrolls, his shadow long against the plastered wall.

dialogue.speaker: kalhana
dialogue.text: I too stand in time’s stream. I will not pretend to stand outside it.

i18n.hi: मैं भी समय की धार में खड़ा हूँ। बाहर खड़े रहने का नाटक नहीं करूँगा।

panels.shot: transition shot: Kalhana in foreground, in background ghostly processions of Karkota kings
panels.action: Kalhana sits to write while behind him, faint, regal figures in ancient Kashmiri dress seem to pass—Lalitaditya and other Karkota rulers—like memories crossing the room.

dialogue.text: Karkota kings are long gone; their palaces ruined, their dates hazy. Yet in the Rajatarangini, they walk again, because for them he alone becomes the storyteller.

i18n.hi: कार्कोट राजाओं को गए ज़माना बीत गया; उनके महल ढह चुके, उनकी तारीखें धुँधली हैं। फिर भी राजतरंगिणी में वे फिर चलते‑फिरते हैं, क्योंकि उनके लिए वही अकेला कथाकार बन जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kalhana pausing over a leaf that mentions vast conquests
panels.action: Kalhana pauses mid-line, stylus raised, as the words “whole earth” appear on the leaf before him, his face caught between admiration and doubt.

dialogue.text: He records claims of Lalitaditya’s vast conquests, yet he is no modern map-maker. Later scholars will test his lines against Tang records, coins, and distant ruins.

i18n.hi: वह ललितादित्य की दूर‑दूर तक फैली विजयों के दावे दर्ज करता है, पर खुद कोई आधुनिक नक्शानवीस नहीं। बाद के विद्वान उसकी पंक्तियों को तांग लिखतों, सिक्कों और दूर के खंडहरों से मिलाकर परखेंगे।

panels.shot: visual blend: Rajatarangini manuscript overlaid with faint Chinese-style court scene and temple ruins
panels.action: A palm-leaf of Rajatarangini fills the frame, while faint images of a Chinese court, a Kashmiri temple ruin, and scattered coins hover like ghostly checks around the text.

dialogue.text: Where foreign records, inscriptions, Martand’s stones, and coins echo his verses, confidence grows. Where only panegyric speaks of ruling the whole earth, doubt must sit beside trust.

i18n.hi: जहाँ विदेशी अभिलेख, शिलालेख, मार्तंड के पत्थर और सिक्के उसकी पद्यधारा को दुहराते हैं, वहाँ भरोसा बढ़ता है। जहाँ केवल प्रशस्ति ही सारी धरती के राज की बात करे, वहाँ भरोसे के पास शक को भी बैठना होगा।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Kalhana’s eyes, tired yet intent
panels.action: Kalhana’s eyes, ringed by work and age, look down with steady resolve, the reflection of a lamp flame flickering in his pupils.

dialogue.text: Kalhana is neither bare myth nor modern historian. He is a careful poet in a 12th-century court, honest about his limits, yet bold enough to judge kings.

i18n.hi: कल्हण न सिर्फ नंगा मिथक है, न ही आधुनिक इतिहासकार। वह बारहवीं सदी के दरबार का सधा हुआ कवि है—अपनी सीमाएँ साफ देखता है, फिर भी राजाओं पर फैसला सुनाने की हिम्मत रखता है।

panels.shot: wide shot: Kalhana placing the finished manuscript among other texts
panels.action: In a broader room, Kalhana sets the tied Rajatarangini bundle onto a shelf beside religious texts and legal documents, then rests his hand lightly upon it.

dialogue.text: By 1149, his river of kings is complete. In it, Kashmir’s past flows from legend through testimony into written memory, ready for future readers to question.

i18n.hi: ११४९ तक उसकी राजाओं की नदी पूरी हो चुकी है। इसमें कश्मीर का बीता समय कथा से गवाही तक, और गवाही से लिखी याद तक बहता है—आने वाले पाठकों की पड़ताल के लिए तैयार।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot: Kalhana framed by window, valley beyond, manuscript in foreground
panels.action: Kalhana sits by an open window overlooking the Kashmir valley, the Rajatarangini bundle before him, mountains and ruins visible in the distance under a pale sky.

dialogue.text: We read Kalhana best when we do as he did: honour the stories, test them against stone and script, and let history be strongest where it admits its sources—and its doubts.

i18n.hi: हम कल्हण को सबसे बेहतर तब पढ़ते हैं जब हम वही करते हैं जो उसने किया: कहानियों का मान रखें, उन्हें पत्थर और लिखत से जाँचें, और इतिहास को वहीं सबसे मजबूत मानें जहाँ वह अपने स्रोत—और अपने शक—खुलकर मान ले।

title_i18n.en: Kalhana Writes the River of Kings
title_i18n.hi: कल्हण की लिखी राजाओं की नदी

subtitle_i18n.en: When a Kashmiri Poet Put Kings on Trial
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब एक कश्मीरी कवि ने राजाओं को कटघरे में खड़ा किया
